name: Carcinosarcoma of the Corpus Uteri
aliases: Malignant Mixed Müllerian Tumor of the Uterus

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in African American women

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Uterine Carcinosarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of both malignant epithelial (carcinomatous) and mesenchymal (sarcomatous) components on histological examination
Immunohistochemical staining demonstrating epithelial markers (e.g., cytokeratin) and mesenchymal markers (e.g., vimentin)
Pelvic imaging (MRI or ultrasound) showing uterine mass with heterogeneous features suggestive of malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of biphasic malignant epithelial and mesenchymal components with supportive immunohistochemical evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other uterine sarcomas and high-grade endometrial carcinomas.

searchTerms: unexpected bleeding from uterus in older women
pelvic mass felt on physical exam

common.symptomName: Pelvic or lower abdominal pain or discomfort
searchTerms: pain or discomfort in pelvis or lower abdomen
fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.symptomName: Urinary frequency or urgency due to mass effect
searchTerms: frequent or urgent urination from mass
urinary symptoms due to pelvic growth

occasional.symptomName: Constipation secondary to pelvic mass compression
searchTerms: constipation caused by pelvic mass pressure
difficulty passing stool due to pelvic compression

occasional.symptomName: Lower extremity edema from lymphatic obstruction
searchTerms: lower limb edema due to lymph obstruction

laboratory: Anemia on complete blood count due to chronic bleeding
Elevated serum calcium in rare paraneoplastic cases
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing heterogeneous uterine mass
MRI pelvis demonstrating invasive uterine tumor with possible myometrial and serosal involvement
CT scan for staging and detection of metastases
other: Histopathology revealing biphasic tumor with carcinomatous and sarcomatous elements
Immunohistochemical dual staining positive for epithelial and mesenchymal markers

distinguishingFeatures: Purely mesenchymal tumor without epithelial elements

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging uterine mass in postmenopausal woman
Evidence of metastatic spread on imaging
references: Amant F, et al. Uterine carcinosarcoma: a review of the literature. Gynecol Oncol. 2009.
